title: 第13章 呼吸奏第14章 昏倒
slug: 我金丹呢你当结石摘出来了
lines: 上午九点整，发令枪响。
人潮涌动。
江城马拉松，三年一度，全城性质的赛事，不设门槛，只要有兴趣就能报名参加，专业选手和业余爱好者同场竞技，赛道从市体育中心出发，沿着江城主干道绕城一圈，全程四十二公里。
起跑线前黑压压的全是人。
专业跑鞋配压缩裤的，普通运动服配帆布鞋的，还有穿着玩偶服来凑热闹的，赛道两侧拉着隔离带，志愿者举着牌子维持秩序，空气里有运动饮料的甜味，也有清晨柏油路被太阳晒热后的淡淡气味。
人群中有一个年轻人，二十五六岁的样子，身材壮硕，肌肉线条分明。
他穿着一身专业马拉松装备，压缩衣、速干短裤、碳板跑鞋，一看就是练家子。
他叫陈锐，省体工队退役的中长跑运动员，现在在江城一家健身房当教练。
这次马拉松，他志在必得。
一方面拿个成绩，另一方面也能给自己的健身房打打广告。
赛前训练了三个月，配速精确到每公里几分几秒，今天的目标，是跑进三小时十分。
发令枪响后，陈锐按照自己的节奏起步。
前一百米，人群还挤在一起，大家都在找位置。
有人跑得太兴奋，手臂甩得很大，有人低头看表，生怕一开始配速飘了，还有人边跑边笑，纯粹当成城市活动来参加。
陈锐呼吸平稳，心率控制在每分钟一百五十次左右。
很标准。
也很稳。
他没有急着往前冲。
马拉松讲的是体力分配，是呼吸节奏，是心率控制。前面跑太猛，后面一定崩，这是铁律。
就在这个时候，他余光里忽然掠过一道白影。
那人没有从赛道最外侧硬冲，也没有夸张地拉开人群。
只是在人流缝隙里轻轻一晃，脚步一变，竟然从几个跑者中间极自然地穿了过去。
陈锐眼神一凝。
白色运动服。
背后印着“江城第一人民医院”的字样。
右手还拎着一个沉甸甸的急救箱。
那箱子随着他手臂微微晃动，看着至少十几公斤，可那人握在手里，竟然像没什么重量。
陈锐下意识看了一眼自己的运动手表。
当前配速，每公里四分半。
而刚才那个人在那短短十几秒里的速度，明显比他快得多。
关键是，对方没有乱。
步频很快。
落地很轻。
上半身甚至没有多余晃动。
这就有点离谱了。
陈锐眉头微微皱起，继续观察。
content_en:
At nine o'clock in the morning, the starting gun sounded.
There was a huge crowd.
The Jiangcheng Marathon is a triennial city-wide event with no threshold. Anyone who is interested can sign up to participate. Professional runners and amateurs compete together. The track starts from the Municipal Sports Center and circles the city along the main road of Jiangcheng, with a total distance of 42 kilometers.
The place in front of the starting line was crowded with people.
There were people wearing professional running shoes and compression pants, ordinary sportswear and canvas shoes, and some wearing doll clothes to join in the fun. There were isolation tapes on both sides of the track, and volunteers held signs to maintain order. There was the sweetness of sports drinks in the air, and the faint smell of the asphalt road being heated by the sun in the early morning.
There was a young man in the crowd, in his mid-twenties, with a strong build and well-defined muscles.
He was wearing professional marathon equipment, including a compression jacket, quick-drying shorts, and carbon-plate running shoes. He looked like a professional athlete at first glance.
His name is Chen Rui, a retired middle-distance runner from the Provincial Sports Team and now a coach at a gym in Jiangcheng.
He is determined to win this marathon.
On the one hand, you can get good results, and on the other hand, you can also advertise your gym.
I trained for three months before the race, and my pace was accurate to a few minutes and seconds per kilometer. Today’s goal is to run within three hours and ten minutes.
After the starting gun sounded, Chen Rui started at his own pace.
For the first hundred meters, the crowd was still crowded together, everyone was looking for a place.
Some people ran so excitedly that they swung their arms wildly, some looked down at their watches for fear that their pace would drift off at the beginning, and some others laughed while running and simply took part in it as a city activity.
Chen Rui's breathing was steady and his heart rate was controlled at about 150 beats per minute.
Very standard.
Very stable too.
He didn't rush forward.
Marathon is about physical distribution, breathing rhythm, and heart rate control. If you run too hard in front, the back will definitely collapse. This is an iron rule.
At this moment, a white shadow suddenly passed through his peripheral vision.
The man did not rush from the outside of the track, nor did he exaggerately pull away from the crowd.
Just a slight sway in the gap in the crowd, a change of pace, and he passed through several runners naturally.
Chen Rui's eyes narrowed.
White sportswear.
The words "Jiangcheng First People's Hospital" are printed on the back.
He was also carrying a heavy first aid kit in his right hand.
The box swayed slightly with his arm, and it looked like it was at least ten kilograms, but when the man held it in his hand, it seemed to weigh nothing.
Chen Rui subconsciously glanced at his sports watch.
Current pace, four and a half minutes per kilometer.
And the speed of the man just now was obviously much faster than him in just ten seconds.
The key is that the other party is not messy.
The cadence is fast.
Landing is light.
There isn't even any unnecessary sway in the upper body.
This is a bit outrageous.
Chen Rui frowned slightly and continued to observe.
